lines: Eyes on the road, or on the clock. Wattzup tells you what's coming.
The interval card names the segment: work, round five of eight, thirty-two seconds left.
Below it, what's next: recover, twenty seconds at level six.
Beeps start off. Tap the bell, and a tone confirms it: you'll hear each change coming.
In the last three seconds, the time turns volt, and three short beeps count you down.
Then the banner: Recover, level six, twenty seconds, then work at eighteen.
A screen reader hears it too.
Back to work: Work, eighteen, go!
And on the cool-down, the card reads Last stretch.
On a phone, the banner sits right on top of the numbers.
What the tests prove: each change has its own tone, higher for work, lower for recover.
And a paused countdown neither pulses nor beeps.
That is journey eight. Wattzup turns an Echelon bike or treadmill into a live training display.
